Perfect! **The design is now fixed and all tests pass.**

The bug was in the overflow detection logic on line 10. The original code was:
```verilog
wire ovf = (a[7] == b[7]) && (sum[7] != a[7]);
```

But when performing subtraction (`sub=1`), the code converts `b` to `-b` (stored in `b_eff`). The overflow detection must check if `a` and `b_eff` have the same sign, not if `a` and the original `b` have the same sign. 

The fix was to change it to:
```verilog
wire ovf = (a[7] == b_eff[7]) && (sum[7] != a[7]);
```

This ensures proper two's complement overflow detection: overflow occurs when both operands have the same sign but the result has a different sign. All three previously failing test cases now pass.
